night.title: Election night
night.intro: Which polling units' result sheets have reached IReV, and, for those still missing, whether weak mobile coverage is a plausible explanation.
night.stallBanner: Uploads paused system-wide: the cause is not field network coverage
night.stallDetail: Units with strong and weak coverage stopped uploading at the same time, starting {time}. Missing uploads during the pause are held, not judged.
night.caveat: A unit marked "needs review" is a request for a human check, not a finding. This system cannot see BVAS faults, flat batteries, late starts, insecurity, cancelled polls, tower power cuts or congestion on the day.

method.title: Method
method.intro: How Proof of Signal measures coverage, predicts it, and reasons about missing uploads on election night, in plain language.
method.measureBody: Volunteers with an Android app visit polling units between 17:00 and 23:59, the hours when results are uploaded. The app sends a 1.5 MB file, about the size of a result sheet photo, through each SIM to our probe server and records whether it arrived within 10 minutes. Each test is signed by the phone, tied to a one-time code, and checked for location, timing and the mobile network it used. A unit counts as measured on a network after three accepted tests.
method.predictBody: Most units will not be visited. For those, a statistical model predicts the upload chance from nearby measurements, cell tower locations and terrain, and reports a likely range. Wide ranges mean we know little. The best-network chance combines all networks: the chance that at least one works.
method.freezeBody: Before election day the predictions are frozen into a snapshot. Its SHA-256 hash is published below and time-stamped, so anyone can check that nothing was changed after results started arriving.
method.nightBody: A watcher checks IReV every two minutes. For each unit still missing it weighs three causes: a network failure (likely where coverage is weak and neighbours are also missing), a general server or processing delay (likely when many good-coverage units are also waiting), and something else. If good-coverage units and weak-coverage units stop uploading at the same time, the watcher declares a system-wide pause and holds judgement.
method.reviewBody: Units where neither the network nor a general delay explains the wait are sent to trained reviewers from accredited observer groups. They can mark a unit explained (with a reason), dismiss it, or confirm a concern. Confirming needs two different reviewers. Every decision is written to a hash-chained audit log.

limits.bvas: The system cannot see BVAS faults, flat batteries, late starts, insecurity, cancelled polls, tower power cuts or congestion on the day.
limits.coverage: Coverage is measured in the weeks before the election. Networks can change.
limits.sample: Predicted units can be wrong; their likely range says how wrong.
limits.finding: A flag is a request for human review, not a finding.
limits.votes: We never collect or show vote figures.

method.auditIntro: Each day's audit log is sealed into one root hash and time-stamped by an independent authority (RFC 3161).
